children: Copper prices gain on better-than-expected economic data in China. Three-month LME prices are 0.8% higher at $14,114 a metric ton after the value of Chinese exports was boosted by higher prices for technology products, ANZ analysts write. This led to a rise in industrial production growth that overshadowed weak domestic demand, they add. Meanwhile, an unexpected influx of the metal into LME warehouses also failed to dent sentiment, the analysts say. (adam.whittaker@wsj.com)
